## The Media tab

The inspector's **Media** tab lists every file the project has imported, in a bar, a find band, the list and a footer.

- **The top bar:** **Add Media…** (⇧⌘I) and a count: "No media", "1 item", "12 items", or "3 of 12 items" while the list is narrowed.
- **The find band:** a **Search by name** field that filters as you type, ignoring case and accents ("resume" finds "Résumé.mov"; Esc clears it), a **Sort** popup (**Import Order**, Name, Duration, Kind), and an **Unused only** checkbox that shows only files no clip uses. Every sort is ascending, and files that tie stay in import order. A file used only inside a nest counts as used. None of these is saved with the project. If nothing matches: "No media matches the search or the filter." If the search or Unused only hides the selected row, that row is deselected.
- **The footer:** **Consolidate…**, with "Copies sources into the package" beside it.

With no media yet, the tab reads "Drop files here, or use Add Media…."

### A media row

Each row shows a thumbnail (a frame for video, a waveform glyph for sound, a cube for a LUT), the file's name, and a line with what applies to that file:

| Kind | The line reads |
|---|---|
| Movie | duration · width×height · frame rate, e.g. `00:01:12:04 · 1920×1080 · 29.97 fps` |
| Picture | width×height |
| Sound | duration |
| LUT | LUT |

Badges on the right mark a file that has **audio** and a file that is **missing**. Hover a row for its tooltip: "Drag to a timeline track, or onto the canvas. Hold ⌥ to insert, ⇧⌥ to overwrite." A LUT's reads "A LUT: apply it to clips as a look." A WebM, MKV or ffmpeg copy's tooltip adds a line above with the original's path and where the copy lives.

Click a row to select it; the selected row is outlined in the accent colour. Selecting a row is not an edit and does not mark the project as changed. Two more sections appear below the list for the selected row when the project has the right kind of file:

- **Camera Log**, once the project has a video file: how the selected file's log footage is converted. See [HDR and colour](hdr-and-color.md).
- **HDR10**, once the project has a PQ file: the peak brightness used for the selected file. See [HDR and colour](hdr-and-color.md).
- **Cursor**, once the project has a video with a picture: the selected screen recording's cursor file — its name, "No cursor file", or the name with "— missing" — with **Locate…** to choose the `.fjcursor` file and **Remove** to forget it. See [Screen recording](screen-recording.md#the-cursor).

### Putting media on the timeline

- **Drag a row onto a timeline track.** With no modifier it lands at the pointer, snapped to a frame, if that part of the track is free; if it would overlap a clip already there, the drop is refused and the drag springs back. Hold **⌥** as you drop to *insert* (the track opens up to make room) or **⇧⌥** to *overwrite* (whatever is under it on that track is replaced).
- **Drag a row onto the canvas.** It lands on a new track at the front, at the playhead.
- **Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead** / **Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead** place the selected row at the playhead. They have no shortcut, and they are off until a row (not a LUT) is selected on the Media tab. The track is the selected clip's track, or the front track when no clip is selected. With a nest open, that is a track inside the nest.

A row can only be placed in its own project's window; dragged into another project's window, it is refused.

A new clip is the whole file, as long as the file runs. A picture is 5 seconds long. With **Fit new clips to canvas** on, a file larger than the canvas is scaled to fit. A LUT row cannot be dragged or placed; it is applied as a look instead. What insert and overwrite do to the clips around them is covered in [Editing](editing.md).

*Agents:* `add_clip`, `insert_clip`, `overwrite_clip` (each takes `track`, `media` and `at`).

### The row's menu

Right-click a row for:

| Item | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Insert at Playhead** | As Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead, for this row. Off for a LUT. |
| **Overwrite at Playhead** | As Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead, for this row. Off for a LUT. |
| **Reveal in Timeline** | Selects every clip on the timeline that shows this file and scrolls to the earliest one; the inspector switches to the Clip tab. Off when nothing on the timeline uses the file, including when its only clips are inside a nest. For a LUT, it selects the clips whose look it is. |
| **Reveal in Finder** | Shows the file in the Finder. For a WebM or MKV copy, shows the original, or the copy when the original is gone. |
| **Relink…** | Points this media at another file (see [Missing media and Relink](#missing-media-and-relink)). |
| **Remove** | Takes the file out of the project (see below). |

### Removing media

**Remove** on an unused file removes it at once, as one undo step. If clips use it, Frame Job asks first:

- For footage: "Remove "*name*"? It is used by 3 clips, which will be removed with it." **Remove and Delete Clips** removes the file and those clips, including any inside nests, as one undo step.
- For a LUT: the alert counts the clips whose look it is ("which keep their place and lose the look") and the files whose Camera Log it is ("which lose it"). **Remove and Clear Looks** removes the LUT and clears those looks and conversions; the clips stay.

Removing media never deletes the file from disk.

*Agents:* `remove_media` (refused while clips use it unless `with_clips: true`).

## Missing media and Relink

A project always opens, even when files it uses have moved or been deleted. Clips whose file is gone keep their place on the timeline and show a slate in their place, and their media rows wear the **missing** badge.

When a project opens with files missing, Frame Job offers the **Missing media** sheet once: "The project opened without these files: their clips keep their place on the timeline and show a slate until the files are found." Each missing file is listed with its old path and a **Locate…** button.

- Choosing a file for one entry also looks in that file's folder for the other missing files by name, and fills in each one it finds. A shoot moved as one folder is usually found with one Locate….
- A located row's button turns into **Change…**.
- The footnote counts the missing files ("3 files").
- **Relink** stays off until at least one file is located, then applies every choice as one undo step ("Relink Media"). You do not have to locate them all: the ones you skip stay missing, and you can relink them later from the Media tab. **Cancel** changes nothing.
- The sheet is offered once, when the window opens, and not over another sheet that is already showing.

Relinking checks the new file as an import does. The media takes the new file's duration, size, frame rate and audio/video flags. A clip that runs past the end of a shorter new file is shortened to end with it. A file of another kind (a sound file for a video entry, say) is refused, and the reason is shown after the other relinks are applied. A WebM or MKV chosen as the new file is copied as on import.

To relink one file at any time, use **Relink…** on its Media-tab row: "Choose the file for "*name*"."

A consolidated package that has been moved or renamed finds its own copies again when it opens: any missing media whose file sits in the package's `media/` folder under the same name is pointed back at it, with no sheet. A screen recording's cursor file is found again the same way.

*Agents:* `relink_media` (takes `media` and `path`; the app checks the new file itself). `get_project`'s `missing_media` lists what needs it.

/// File ▸ Consolidate Media… — copies every file the project references into
/// `media/` inside the `.framejob` package and relinks the project at the

///
/// Frame Job REFERENCES media by default (§4.2, §11): a project is a small
/// JSON file pointing at whatever the footage happens to live on. Consolidate
/// is the one command that trades that for self-containment — the package
/// becomes the whole edit, so it can be handed to someone else or archived
/// with its sources deleted.
///
/// This type is the engine and nothing else: it plans, it copies, and it
/// hands back the `relink_media` ops it earned. Applying them is the
/// caller's job — `EditorViewController+Consolidate.swift` through
/// `ProjectDocument`, `AgentServer+Media.swift` through `editResult` — so
/// there is still exactly one mutation point.
///
/// **Four traps, all of them load-bearing.**
///
/// 1. *An untitled project has no package to copy into.* `plan` refuses it
///    rather than inventing a destination: `ProjectDocument`'s temporary
///    cache directory is documented as orphanable, and orphaning a cache
///    costs a filmstrip where orphaning MEDIA loses the file.
/// 2. *Two files can share a basename.* Names are claimed against the
///    directory's existing contents and against each other, case-insensitively
///    (the volume usually is), so `intro.mov` and `b-roll/intro.mov` become
///    `intro.mov` and `intro-2.mov`.
/// 3. *A file already inside the package must not be copied onto itself.*
///    Those entries are relinked but never copied — and relinking them still
///    matters, because a stale BOOKMARK pointing outside the package wins
///    over the path in `mediaURL(for:)`.

---
title: "The Media tab"
description: "Find, read and manage every file a project has imported, from the list on the inspector's Media tab."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The **Media** tab is the project's library: every file you've imported, whether a clip uses it or not. Come here to find a file, see what it is, put it on the timeline, or sort out one that has gone missing.

<AtAGlance
  where={['Inspector ▸ Media', 'Right-click a row for its menu']}
  tools={['get_project', 'insert_clip', 'overwrite_clip', 'set_selection', 'relink_media', 'remove_media']}
/>

<Shot
  name="10b-media-tab.inspector"
  alt="The Media tab with three files. At the top, an Add Media… button with its shortcut ⇧⌘I and the count 3 items. Below it a Search by name field, a Sort popup set to Import Order and an Unused only checkbox. The rows show speech.mov with a thumbnail and the line 00:00:05:07 · 640×360 · 30 f…, and toneA.m4a and toneB.m4a with a waveform glyph and their durations, all three with a green audio badge. A Consolidate… button sits under the list, followed by the Camera Log and Cursor sections."
/>

## What the tab shows

A project points at your files where they are, and doesn't copy them in. That's why a row can be missing, and why the tab offers **Relink…** and **Consolidate…**.

From top to bottom, the tab holds:

- **The top bar:** **Add Media…** (<kbd>⇧⌘I</kbd>) and [the item count](#the-item-count). See [Import media](/projects/import-media/). You can also drop files from the Finder onto the tab to add them.
- **The find band:** [a search field](#search-by-name), [a sort](#sort) and [Unused only](#unused-only). With no media yet, this band isn't there and the tab reads "Drop files here, or use Add Media…."
- **The list:** one row per file.
- **The footer:** **Consolidate…**, with the line "Copies sources into the package". See [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/).

Three more sections sit under the list and work on the [selected row](#select-a-row):

| Section | Appears once the project has | See |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Camera Log** | A video file | [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/) |
| **HDR10** | A PQ file | [HDR10 peak](/hdr/hdr10-peak/) |
| **Cursor** | A video with a picture | [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/) |

## Read a row

Each row has a thumbnail, the file's name, and a line of facts that depends on the kind of file.

| Kind | Thumbnail | The line reads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Movie | A frame from the movie | Duration, size and frame rate, such as `00:01:12:04 · 1920×1080 · 29.97 fps` |
| Picture | The picture | Width × height, such as `3024×4032` |
| Sound | A waveform glyph | Duration |
| LUT | A cube glyph | `LUT` |

A file with no duration or size shows its kind instead. Thumbnails arrive a moment after an import, and until then a glyph stands in. A line too long for the row ends in an ellipsis, so widen the inspector to read the rest.

### Badges

Badges sit at the right of a row:

- **audio**, in green, marks a file with sound.

| --- | --- |

---
title: "Remove media"
description: "Take a file out of a project from the Media tab, with or without the clips that use it, and leave it safe on disk."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Removing media takes a file off the project's list. It never touches the file on your disk, and one undo brings it back.

<AtAGlance
  where="Right-click a row on the Media tab ▸ Remove"
  tools="remove_media"
/>

## Remove a file

Right-click the file's row on the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) and choose **Remove**.

If no clip uses the file, it goes at once, with no question, as one undo step called **Remove Media**.

To see what you can remove without losing a clip, tick [Unused only](/projects/media-tab/#unused-only) first.

## Remove a file clips use

If clips use the file, Frame Job asks first, because a clip can't stay in a project without its file. The alert reads "Remove “name”? It is used by 3 clips, which will be removed with it."

- **Remove and Delete Clips** removes the file and those clips as one undo step.
- **Cancel** changes nothing.

The count covers the whole project, including clips inside [nests](/editing/nests/), even while a nest is open. The clips go from wherever they are:

- Clips on the timeline leave their time empty. The clips around them don't move.
- Clips inside a nest go from the nest. The nest itself stays, with everything else in it.

If you'd rather keep the clips and use another file, [relink](/projects/relink-media/#relink-one-file) instead.

## What stays on disk

Remove never deletes a file:

- Your original stays where it is.
- A copy in the project's package, from [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/), stays in the package's `media` folder.
- A movie copy Frame Job made of a [WebM or MKV](/projects/webm-and-matroska/) stays in its Rewrapped folder.

## Good to know

- Removing a LUT works differently: its clips stay and lose their look. See [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/).
- A clip set to [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/) by following the removed file stops hiding. The clip stays.
- Remove works with a nest open, and it changes the whole project.

## With an agent

`remove_media` doesn't ask. It won't remove a file that clips still use unless the call says to take the clips too, and otherwise it answers with the clips in the way. See [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/).

## Related

- [The Media tab](/projects/media-tab/)
- [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/)
- [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/)

---
title: "Relink missing media"
description: "Point a project back at files that have moved, one at a time or a whole folder at once, and see what a relink changes and keeps."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A project points at your files where they are, so moving or deleting one leaves its clips with nothing to show. Relinking tells Frame Job where the file is now, or gives it another file to use instead.

<AtAGlance
  where={['The Missing media sheet, when a project opens', 'Right-click a row on the Media tab ▸ Relink…']}
  tools={['relink_media', 'get_project']}
/>

## When a file goes missing

A project always opens, even with files gone. For each missing file:

- Its clips keep their place on the timeline and show a slate, with no sound.
- Its row on the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) wears a coral **missing** badge.
- An export still runs, and writes the slate and silence for those clips.

Frame Job remembers a file by more than its path, so one you've moved or renamed is often still found and never shows as missing.

## Relink from the Missing media sheet

When a project opens with files missing, the **Missing media** sheet comes up, once. It reads "The project opened without these files: their clips keep their place on the timeline and show a slate until the files are found." Each file is listed with its old path, and the footnote counts them ("3 files").

<Steps>

1. Choose **Locate…** beside a file.

2. Pick its new location in the panel, which reads "Choose the file for “name”." Its path appears in the row, and the button turns into **Change…**.

3. Check the other rows. Frame Job has [looked in the same folder](#locate-one-file-find-the-rest) for them.

4. Choose **Relink**.

</Steps>

**Relink** stays off until at least one file is located, then applies every choice as one undo step called **Relink Media**. You don't have to locate them all. The ones you skip stay missing, and you can [relink them later](#relink-one-file). **Cancel** changes nothing.

The sheet is offered once per project window, when it opens, and doesn't appear over another sheet. After that, use the Media tab.

### Locate one file, find the rest

Choosing a file also looks in that file's folder for the other missing files, by name. So a shoot moved as one folder is usually found with one **Locate…**.

Only the folder you pointed at is searched. A row is filled only if a file of that name is there, and a row that already has a file keeps it.

## Relink one file

To relink at any time, right-click the file's row on the Media tab, choose **Relink…**, and pick the file in the panel, which reads "Choose the file for “name”."

This works for any file, missing or not, so you can use it to swap one file for another across every clip that shows it. It's one undo step, **Relink Media**. Thumbnails and waveforms are rebuilt if the new file is a different one, and a file that has only moved keeps them.

## What Frame Job checks

The new file is read as an import reads it:

- **It must be the same kind of file.** You can't relink a movie to a sound file, for example. From the Media tab you get a beep and the reason at the foot of the inspector. In the sheet, the other relinks are applied first and then an alert gives the reason. The file stays missing either way.
- **It must be readable.** A file Frame Job can't open brings up an alert, and the sheet's other choices still go through.
- **A WebM or MKV is copied as it is on import.** See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/). Choosing **Cancel** during the copy leaves that file out of the relink. A file macOS can't open can go through the same [ffmpeg step](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) as an import.

## What a relink changes

The entry takes the new file's duration, size, frame rate, and whether it has audio, video and alpha.

A clip that runs past the end of a shorter new file is shortened to end with it, on the timeline and inside [nests](/editing/nests/). A clip that starts past the new end keeps a single frame. Nothing else on the timeline moves, and everything else about the clip stays as it was.

A relink also starts the file's analysis again, so features that use it wait for the new answers. [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) is one.

## What a relink keeps

Some things belong to the entry rather than to the file, so they carry over:

| What | After a relink |
| --- | --- |
| [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/) | Kept. It's your reading of the footage, which a new path doesn't change. |
| [HDR10 peak](/hdr/hdr10-peak/) | Kept. The peak is read only at import, so set it by hand if the new file differs. |
| [Cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) | The one beside the new movie is taken. If there's none, the existing one stays, as long as it's still there and the new movie is the same size. Otherwise the media has no cursor file. |
| Saved speech, for [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/) | What still fits in the new file is kept. A new file with no sound forgets it. |

## Good to know

- A file in the Trash isn't missing yet. Frame Job follows it there and keeps playing it until you empty the Trash.
- A project opened from a consolidated package that has moved finds its own copies, with no sheet. See [Move a consolidated package](/projects/consolidate-media/#move-a-consolidated-package).
- If a WebM or MKV copy has gone but the original is still there, Frame Job makes the copy again when the project opens. See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/).
- A relink stores what Frame Job needs to follow the file, so the next move is followed too.
- Relinking works with a nest open, and it changes the whole project.

## With an agent

`get_project` lists the entries that need relinking under `missing_media`, and `relink_media` points one at a file, with the same checks. It takes one file at a time and doesn't search a folder. See [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/).

## Related

- [The Media tab](/projects/media-tab/)
- [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/)
- [Import media](/projects/import-media/)

Choosing a file also looks in that file's folder for the other missing files, by name. So a shoot moved as one folder is usually found with one **Locate…**.

Only the folder you pointed at is searched. A row is filled only if a file of that name is there, and a row that already has a file keeps it.

## Relink one file

To relink at any time, right-click the file's row on the Media tab, choose **Relink…**, and pick the file in the panel, which reads "Choose the file for “name”."

This works for any file, missing or not, so you can use it to swap one file for another across every clip that shows it. It's one undo step, **Relink Media**. Thumbnails and waveforms are rebuilt if the new file is a different one, and a file that has only moved keeps them.

## What Frame Job checks

The new file is read as an import reads it:

- **It must be the same kind of file.** You can't relink a movie to a sound file, for example. From the Media tab you get a beep and the reason at the foot of the inspector. In the sheet, the other relinks are applied first and then an alert gives the reason. The file stays missing either way.
- **It must be readable.** A file Frame Job can't open brings up an alert, and the sheet's other choices still go through.
- **A WebM or MKV is copied as it is on import.** See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/). Choosing **Cancel** during the copy leaves that file out of the relink. A file macOS can't open can go through the same [ffmpeg step](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) as an import.

## What a relink changes

The entry takes the new file's duration, size, frame rate, and whether it has audio, video and alpha.

A clip that runs past the end of a shorter new file is shortened to end with it, on the timeline and inside [nests](/editing/nests/). A clip that starts past the new end keeps a single frame. Nothing else on the timeline moves, and everything else about the clip stays as it was.

A relink also starts the file's analysis again, so features that use it wait for the new answers. [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) is one.

## What a relink keeps

Some things belong to the entry rather than to the file, so they carry over:

| What | After a relink |
| --- | --- |
| [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/) | Kept. It's your reading of the footage, which a new path doesn't change. |
| [HDR10 peak](/hdr/hdr10-peak/) | Kept. The peak is read only at import, so set it by hand if the new file differs. |
| [Cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) | The one beside the new movie is taken. If there's none, the existing one stays, as long as it's still there and the new movie is the same size. Otherwise the media has no cursor file. |
| Saved speech, for [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/) | What still fits in the new file is kept. A new file with no sound forgets it. |

## Good to know

- A file in the Trash isn't missing yet. Frame Job follows it there and keeps playing it until you empty the Trash.
- A project opened from a consolidated package that has moved finds its own copies, with no sheet. See [Move a consolidated package](/projects/consolidate-media/#move-a-consolidated-package).
- If a WebM or MKV copy has gone but the original is still there, Frame Job makes the copy again when the project opens. See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/).
- A relink stores what Frame Job needs to follow the file, so the next move is followed too.
- Relinking works with a nest open, and it changes the whole project.

## With an agent

`get_project` lists the entries that need relinking under `missing_media`, and `relink_media` points one at a file, with the same checks. It takes one file at a time and doesn't search a folder. See [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/).

## Related

- [The Media tab](/projects/media-tab/)
- [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/)
- [Import media](/projects/import-media/)

---
title: "Consolidate Media"
description: "Copy every file a project uses into its package, so you can hand it over, move it or archive it without the originals."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A project normally points at your files where they are. Consolidate Media copies them all into the `.framejob` package and points the project at the copies, so the package becomes the whole edit. You can then hand it to someone, move it, or archive it and delete the originals.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Consolidate Media…"
  where="Media tab footer ▸ Consolidate…"
  tools="consolidate_media"
  needs="A saved project, and room on the disk for a second copy of the footage."
/>

## Consolidate a project

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Consolidate Media…**, or **Consolidate…** at the foot of the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/). Both are off when the project has no media.

2. Watch the **Consolidating Media** sheet as the files copy.

3. Read what the sheet reports, then choose **Close**, or **Show in Finder** to see the copies.

</Steps>

Every file in the media list is copied into a `media` folder inside the package, whether a clip uses it or not. To keep the package smaller, [remove](/projects/remove-media/) what you don't need first. [Unused only](/projects/media-tab/#unused-only) shows you what that is.

## Save the project first

An untitled project has no package to copy into. On one, the command asks "Save this project first?" and offers **Save…** and **Cancel**. After the save it carries on where it left off. Cancelling the Save panel stops the command.

## While it copies

The sheet shows a bar, a line such as "Copying 4 files (2.1 GB) into the package…", and the name of the file being copied. When every file is already inside and only the project's links need correcting, the line reads "Relinking 2…".

**Cancel** stops between files, so the sheet shows "Stopping…" until the file in progress is done. What was copied stays copied and the project points at it, and the rest keep pointing at the originals. The project always opens. Run the command again to copy the rest.

## When it finishes

The sheet says what happened, offers **Show in Finder** and **Close**, and the changes to the project are one undo step called **Consolidate Media**. **Show in Finder** shows the package's `media` folder and closes the sheet.

| The sheet says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Copied 4 files (2.1 GB) into the package." | How many files it copied, cursor files included. |
| "No files needed copying." | Nothing was copied, and only links were corrected. |
| "Stopped before the rest." | You chose **Cancel**. |
| "2 files could not be copied." | Those files keep pointing at their originals, so every clip still plays. The first file's reason shows underneath. |
| "1 missing file was left alone — relink intro.mov." | See [Missing files](#missing-files). It names up to three. |
| "1 cursor file was missing and left alone." | See [Cursor files](#cursor-files). |

## What gets copied

### Names and duplicates

- Two different files with the same name are kept apart, as `intro.mov` and `intro-2.mov`. Names are compared without regard to case, and a name already in the `media` folder counts as taken.
- Two media entries for one file share a single copy.
- Files already inside the package aren't copied again.

### Missing files

A missing file can't be copied, so it's left alone and the sheet names it. [Relink it](/projects/relink-media/) and consolidate again.

With nothing to do, Frame Job doesn't open the sheet. It shows an alert reading "Nothing to consolidate." and why:

- "Every file this project uses is already inside the package."
- "Every file this project can find is already inside the package. 2 missing files need relinking first."

### LUTs

[LUTs](/color/luts/) are consolidated like footage.

### Cursor files

A screen recording's [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) is copied too, next to its movie and named after it: `Recording.mov` and `Recording.fjcursor`. It counts as one of the files copied in the final report.

- It's copied only once its movie is, and the project points at the copy only once it's there.
- One that can't be copied is listed with the other failures, and the recording keeps its original cursor file.
- One that's missing is left alone: "1 cursor file was missing and left alone."

### WebM, MKV and converted files

For a [WebM or MKV](/projects/webm-and-matroska/), or a file [converted with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/), Frame Job copies the movie it plays from, not the file you imported. The row's [tooltip](/projects/media-tab/#the-tooltip) then says it was copied into this project's package.

## Move a consolidated package

Move or rename a consolidated package and it finds its own copies when it opens. Any missing file with a file of the same name in the package's `media` folder is pointed back at it, and a screen recording's cursor file is found again the same way.

This happens with no sheet, and it isn't an edit, so it adds no undo step. A file that still resolves is never touched, even if a file of the same name sits in `media`. Anything still missing after this brings up the [Missing media sheet](/projects/relink-media/#relink-from-the-missing-media-sheet).

## Good to know

- Nothing checks for free space first. A copy that runs out of room is reported with the files that couldn't be copied, and those files keep pointing at their originals.
- Undo points the project back at the originals but leaves the copies in the package. Consolidating again then makes second copies, such as `intro-2.mov`.
- A file that can't be copied leaves two entries that share it on the original, both of them.

## With an agent

`consolidate_media` does the same work with no sheet and no **Cancel**, and Frame Job's own window doesn't respond until the copy is done, which can take a while. On a project that has never been saved it stops and says to save first. The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) asks you before it runs it. See [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/).

## Related

- [The Media tab](/projects/media-tab/)
- [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/)
- [Remove media](/projects/remove-media/)
- [Save, revert and close](/projects/save-and-revert/)

17	## Add a marker
18	
19	Move the playhead to the moment and press <kbd>M</kbd>. The bookmark button in the timeline bar and **Mark ▸ Add Marker** do the same.

21	A new marker is red and is called `Marker 1`, `Marker 2` and so on. Two markers can't share a frame, so pressing <kbd>M</kbd> on a frame that already has one beeps and adds nothing.
22

29	| Move a marker | Drag its flag along the ruler. It snaps, and it won't land on a frame that already has a marker. |

31	| Remove a marker | Choose **Delete** in its row in the Document tab. |

The name field in the Document tab is different: empty it and the marker has no name, and the field shows **Marker** in grey.

38

...

---
title: "The Media tab"
description: "Find, read and manage every file a project has imported, from the list on the inspector's Media tab."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The **Media** tab is the project's library: every file you've imported, whether a clip uses it or not. Come here to find a file, see what it is, put it on the timeline, or sort out one that has gone missing.

<AtAGlance
  where={['Inspector ▸ Media', 'Right-click a row for its menu']}
  tools={['get_project', 'insert_clip', 'overwrite_clip', 'set_selection', 'relink_media', 'remove_media']}
/>

<Shot
  name="10b-media-tab.inspector"
  alt="The Media tab with three files. At the top, an Add Media… button with its shortcut ⇧⌘I and the count 3 items. Below it a Search by name field, a Sort popup set to Import Order and an Unused only checkbox. The rows show speech.mov with a thumbnail and the line 00:00:05:07 · 640×360 · 30 f…, and toneA.m4a and toneB.m4a with a waveform glyph and their durations, all three with a green audio badge. A Consolidate… button sits under the list, followed by the Camera Log and Cursor sections."
/>

## What the tab shows

A project points at your files where they are, and doesn't copy them in. That's why a row can be missing, and why the tab offers **Relink…** and **Consolidate…**.

From top to bottom, the tab holds:

- **The top bar:** **Add Media…** (<kbd>⇧⌘I</kbd>) and [the item count](#the-item-count). See [Import media](/projects/import-media/). You can also drop files from the Finder onto the tab to add them.
- **The find band:** [a search field](#search-by-name), [a sort](#sort) and [Unused only](#unused-only). With no media yet, this band isn't there and the tab reads "Drop files here, or use Add Media…."
- **The list:** one row per file.
- **The footer:** **Consolidate…**, with the line "Copies sources into the package". See [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/).

Three more sections sit under the list and work on the [selected row](#select-a-row):

| Section | Appears once the project has | See |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Camera Log** | A video file | [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/) |
| **HDR10** | A PQ file | [HDR10 peak](/hdr/hdr10-peak/) |
| **Cursor** | A video with a picture | [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/) |

## Read a row

Each row has a thumbnail, the file's name, and a line of facts that depends on the kind of file.

| Kind | Thumbnail | The line reads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Movie | A frame from the movie | Duration, size and frame rate, such as `00:01:12:04 · 1920×1080 · 29.97 fps` |
| Picture | The picture | Width × height, such as `3024×4032` |
| Sound | A waveform glyph | Duration |
| LUT | A cube glyph | `LUT` |

A file with no duration or size shows its kind instead. Thumbnails arrive a moment after an import, and until then a glyph stands in. A line too long for the row ends in an ellipsis, so widen the inspector to read the rest.

### Badges

Badges sit at the right of a row:

- **audio**, in green, marks a file with sound.
- **missing**, in coral, marks a file Frame Job can't find. It's always shown, however little room the row has, because the name and the line give way first. See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).

### The tooltip

Hover over a row to see how to place it: "Drag to a timeline track, or onto the canvas. Hold ⌥ to insert, ⇧⌥ to overwrite."

A LUT's tooltip reads "A LUT: apply it to clips as a look."

A file Frame Job made a movie copy of, such as a [WebM or MKV](/projects/webm-and-matroska/) or a [conversion with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/), has one more line above that. It gives the original's path and where the copy lives: Frame Job's Rewrapped folder, or this project's package once you've [consolidated](/projects/consolidate-media/#webm-mkv-and-converted-files).

## Find a file

### Search by name

Type in **Search by name** and the list narrows as you type. It ignores case and accents, as the Finder does, so "resume" finds "Résumé.mov". Every character you type counts, including a space. Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to clear the field.

If nothing matches, or nothing is left once [Unused only](#unused-only) is on too, the tab reads "No media matches the search or the filter."

### Sort

The **Sort** popup puts the list in one of four orders. The default is **Import Order**.

| Sort | Order |
| --- | --- |
| **Import Order** | The order the files were added. |
| **Name** | Alphabetical, the way the Finder sorts, so `clip2` comes before `clip10`. |
| **Duration** | Shortest first. Pictures and LUTs have no duration, so they come first. |
| **Kind** | Audio, Image, LUT, then Video. |

Every order is ascending, and files that tie stay in import order.

### Unused only

Tick **Unused only** to show only the files no clip uses. It's a quick way to see what you could [remove](/projects/remove-media/) before you hand a project on.

- A file used only inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) counts as used.
- A LUT counts as used when it's a clip's look or a file's Camera Log. A LUT that only an action's end names counts as unused.

### The item count

The top bar counts the files, and how many are showing while the list is narrowed:

| Count | Means |
| --- | --- |
| No media | The project has no files. |
| 1 item, 12 items | Every file is showing. |
| 3 of 12 items | A search or Unused only is hiding the rest. |

The search, the sort and Unused only belong to the window. They aren't saved with the project, and each open project has its own. They do survive an import, so a search stays on while you add more files.

## Select a row

Click a row to select it. The row gets an outline in the accent colour, and it becomes the file these work on:

- **Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead** and **Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead**, which stay off until a row other than a LUT is selected. See [Add clips to the timeline](/editing/add-clips/).
- The Camera Log, HDR10 and Cursor sections under the list.

Selecting a row isn't an edit. It adds no undo step and doesn't mark the project as changed. If a search or Unused only hides the selected row, the row is deselected, so you can't place a file you can't see.

## The row's menu

Right-click a row for its menu. It acts on the row you clicked, whatever the selected row is.

| Item | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Insert at Playhead** | Places the file at the playhead and makes room for it. Off for a LUT. |
| **Overwrite at Playhead** | Places the file at the playhead and takes the room it needs. Off for a LUT. |
| **Reveal in Timeline** | Selects the clips showing this file. See [below](#reveal-in-timeline). |
| **Reveal in Finder** | Shows the file in the Finder. See [below](#reveal-in-finder). |
| **Relink…** | Points this entry at another file. See [Relink one file](/projects/relink-media/#relink-one-file). |
| **Remove** | Takes the file out of the project. See [Remove media](/projects/remove-media/). |

**Insert at Playhead** and **Overwrite at Playhead** also select the row. They use the same track as the **Edit** menu's items, the selected clip's track or else the front track, and [Add clips to the timeline](/editing/add-clips/) has the rest. A LUT is never placed, because it's [applied as a look](/color/luts/). A LUT row doesn't drag either.

### Reveal in Timeline

**Reveal in Timeline** answers "where did I use this?". It selects every clip showing the file, scrolls to the earliest one, and the inspector switches to the Clip tab. For a LUT, it selects the clips whose look it is.

The item is off when nothing in the timeline itself uses the file, and that includes a file whose only clips are inside a nest. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> first: the command looks at whatever's open, so it then finds the clips in there.

Revealing clips changes the selection, not the project. It adds no undo step.

### Reveal in Finder

**Reveal in Finder** shows the file in the Finder. For a WebM, an MKV or another file Frame Job made a copy of, it shows the original, or the copy when the original has gone. With neither on disk, it beeps.

- [Import media](/projects/import-media/)

- [Remove media](/projects/remove-media/)
- [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/)
- [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/)

---
title: "Remove media"
description: "Take a file out of a project from the Media tab, with or without the clips that use it, and leave it safe on disk."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Removing media takes a file off the project's list. It never touches the file on your disk, and one undo brings it back.

<AtAGlance
  where="Right-click a row on the Media tab ▸ Remove"
  tools="remove_media"
/>

## Remove a file

Right-click the file's row on the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) and choose **Remove**.

If no clip uses the file, it goes at once, with no question, as one undo step called **Remove Media**.

To see what you can remove without losing a clip, tick [Unused only](/projects/media-tab/#unused-only) first.

## Remove a file clips use

If clips use the file, Frame Job asks first, because a clip can't stay in a project without its file. The alert reads "Remove “name”? It is used by 3 clips, which will be removed with it."

- **Remove and Delete Clips** removes the file and those clips as one undo step.
- **Cancel** changes nothing.

The count covers the whole project, including clips inside [nests](/editing/nests/), even while a nest is open. The clips go from wherever they are:

- Clips on the timeline leave their time empty. The clips around them don't move.
- Clips inside a nest go from the nest. The nest itself stays, with everything else in it.

If you'd rather keep the clips and use another file, [relink](/projects/relink-media/#relink-one-file) instead.

## What stays on disk

Remove never deletes a file:

- Your original stays where it is.
- A copy in the project's package, from [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/), stays in the package's `media` folder.
- A movie copy Frame Job made of a [WebM or MKV](/projects/webm-and-matroska/) stays in its Rewrapped folder.

## Good to know

- Removing a LUT works differently: its clips stay and lose their look. See [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/).
- A clip set to [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/) by following the removed file stops hiding. The clip stays.
- Remove works with a nest open, and it changes the whole project.

## With an agent

`remove_media` doesn't ask. It won't remove a file that clips still use unless the call says to take the clips too, and otherwise it answers with the clips in the way. See [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/).

## Related

- [The Media tab](/projects/media-tab/)
- [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/)
- [Delete, Ripple Delete and Lift](/editing/delete-clips/)

---
title: "Relink missing media"
description: "Point a project back at files that have moved, one at a time or a whole folder at once, and see what a relink changes and keeps."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A project points at your files where they are, so moving or deleting one leaves its clips with nothing to show. Relinking tells Frame Job where the file is now, or gives it another file to use instead.

<AtAGlance
  where={['The Missing media sheet, when a project opens', 'Right-click a row on the Media tab ▸ Relink…']}
  tools={['relink_media', 'get_project']}
/>

## When a file goes missing

A project always opens, even with files gone. For each missing file:

- Its clips keep their place on the timeline and show a slate, with no sound.
- Its row on the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) wears a coral **missing** badge.
- An export still runs, and writes the slate and silence for those clips.

Frame Job remembers a file by more than its path, so one you've moved or renamed is often still found and never shows as missing.

## Relink from the Missing media sheet

When a project opens with files missing, the **Missing media** sheet comes up, once. It reads "The project opened without these files: their clips keep their place on the timeline and show a slate until the files are found." Each file is listed with its old path, and the footnote counts them ("3 files").

<Steps>

1. Choose **Locate…** beside a file.

2. Pick its new location in the panel, which reads "Choose the file for “name”." Its path appears in the row, and the button turns into **Change…**.

3. Check the other rows. Frame Job has [looked in the same folder](#locate-one-file-find-the-rest) for them.

4. Choose **Relink**.

</Steps>

**Relink** stays off until at least one file is located, then applies every choice as one undo step called **Relink Media**. You don't have to locate them all. The ones you skip stay missing, and you can [relink them later](#relink-one-file). **Cancel** changes nothing.

The sheet is offered once per project window, when it opens, and doesn't appear over another sheet. After that, use the Media tab.

### Locate one file, find the rest

Choosing a file also looks in that file's folder for the other missing files, by name. So a shoot moved as one folder is usually found with one **Locate…**.

Only the folder you pointed at is searched. A row is filled only if a file of that name is there, and a row that already has a file keeps it.

## Relink one file

To relink at any time, right-click the file's row on the Media tab, choose **Relink…**, and pick the file in the panel, which reads "Choose the file for “name”."

This works for any file, missing or not, so you can use it to swap one file for another across every clip that shows it. It's one undo step, **Relink Media**. Thumbnails and waveforms are rebuilt if the new file is a different one, and a file that has only moved keeps them.

## What Frame Job checks

The new file is read as an import reads it:

- **It must be the same kind of file.** You can't relink a movie to a sound file, for example. From the Media tab you get a beep and the reason at the foot of the inspector. In the sheet, the other relinks are applied first and then an alert gives the reason. The file stays missing either way.
- **It must be readable.** A file Frame Job can't open brings up an alert, and the sheet's other choices still go through.
- **A WebM or MKV is copied as it is on import.** See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/). Choosing **Cancel** during the copy leaves that file out of the relink. A file macOS can't open can go through the same [ffmpeg step](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) as an import.

## What a relink changes

The entry takes the new file's duration, size, frame rate, and whether it has audio, video and alpha.

A clip that runs past the end of a shorter new file is shortened to end with it, on the timeline and inside [nests](/editing/nests/). A clip that starts past the new end keeps a single frame. Nothing else on the timeline moves, and everything else about the clip stays as it was.

A relink also starts the file's analysis again, so features that use it wait for the new answers. [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) is one.

## What a relink keeps

Some things belong to the entry rather than to the file, so they carry over:

| What | After a relink |
| --- | --- |
| [Camera Log](/hdr/camera-log/) | Kept. It's your reading of the footage, which a new path doesn't change. |
| [HDR10 peak](/hdr/hdr10-peak/) | Kept. The peak is read only at import, so set it by hand if the new file differs. |
| [Cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) | The one beside the new movie is taken. If there's none, the existing one stays, as long as it's still there and the new movie is the same size. Otherwise the media has no cursor file. |
| Saved speech, for [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/) | What still fits in the new file is kept. A new file with no sound forgets it. |

## Good to know

- A file in the Trash isn't missing yet. Frame Job follows it there and keeps playing it until you empty the Trash.
- A project opened from a consolidated package that has moved finds its own copies, with no sheet. See [Move a consolidated package](/projects/consolidate-media/#move-a-consolidated-package).
- If a WebM or MKV copy has gone but the original is still there, Frame Job makes the copy again when the project opens. See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/).
- A relink stores what Frame Job needs to follow the file, so the next move is followed too.
- Relinking works with a nest open, and it changes the whole project.

## With an agent

`get_project` lists the entries that need relinking under `missing_media`, and `relink_media` points one at a file, with the same checks. It takes one file at a time and doesn't search a folder. See [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/).

## Related

- [The Media tab](/projects/media-tab/)
- [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/)
- [Import media](/projects/import-media/)

---
title: "Consolidate Media"
description: "Copy every file a project uses into its package, so you can hand it over, move it or archive it without the originals."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A project normally points at your files where they are. Consolidate Media copies them all into the `.framejob` package and points the project at the copies, so the package becomes the whole edit. You can then hand it to someone, move it, or archive it and delete the originals.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Consolidate Media…"
  where="Media tab footer ▸ Consolidate…"
  tools="consolidate_media"
  needs="A saved project, and room on the disk for a second copy of the footage."
/>

## Consolidate a project

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Consolidate Media…**, or **Consolidate…** at the foot of the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/). Both are off when the project has no media.

2. Watch the **Consolidating Media** sheet as the files copy.

3. Read what the sheet reports, then choose **Close**, or **Show in Finder** to see the copies.

</Steps>

Every file in the media list is copied into a `media` folder inside the package, whether a clip uses it or not. To keep the package smaller, [remove](/projects/remove-media/) what you don't need first. [Unused only](/projects/media-tab/#unused-only) shows you what that is.

## Save the project first

An untitled project has no package to copy into. On one, the command asks "Save this project first?" and offers **Save…** and **Cancel**. After the save it carries on where it left off. Cancelling the Save panel stops the command.

## While it copies

The sheet shows a bar, a line such as "Copying 4 files (2.1 GB) into the package…", and the name of the file being copied. When every file is already inside and only the project's links need correcting, the line reads "Relinking 2…".

**Cancel** stops between files, so the sheet shows "Stopping…" until the file in progress is done. What was copied stays copied and the project points at it, and the rest keep pointing at the originals. The project always opens. Run the command again to copy the rest.

## When it finishes

The sheet says what happened, offers **Show in Finder** and **Close**, and the changes to the project are one undo step called **Consolidate Media**. **Show in Finder** shows the package's `media` folder and closes the sheet.

| The sheet says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Copied 4 files (2.1 GB) into the package." | How many files it copied, cursor files included. |
| "No files needed copying." | Nothing was copied, and only links were corrected. |
| "Stopped before the rest." | You chose **Cancel**. |
| "2 files could not be copied." | Those files keep pointing at their originals, so every clip still plays. The first file's reason shows underneath. |
| "1 missing file was left alone — relink intro.mov." | See [Missing files](#missing-files). It names up to three. |
| "1 cursor file was missing and left alone." | See [Cursor files](#cursor-files). |

## What gets copied

### Names and duplicates

- Two different files with the same name are kept apart, as `intro.mov` and `intro-2.mov`. Names are compared without regard to case, and a name already in the `media` folder counts as taken.
- Two media entries for one file share a single copy.
- Files already inside the package aren't copied again.

### Missing files

A missing file can't be copied, so it's left alone and the sheet names it. [Relink it](/projects/relink-media/) and consolidate again.

With nothing to do, Frame Job doesn't open the sheet. It shows an alert reading "Nothing to consolidate." and why:

- "Every file this project uses is already inside the package."
- "Every file this project can find is already inside the package. 2 missing files need relinking first."

### LUTs

[LUTs](/color/luts/) are consolidated like footage.

### Cursor files

A screen recording's [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) is copied too, next to its movie and named after it: `Recording.mov` and `Recording.fjcursor`. It counts as one of the files copied in the final report.

- It's copied only once its movie is, and the project points at the copy only once it's there.
- One that can't be copied is listed with the other failures, and the recording keeps its original cursor file.
- One that's missing is left alone: "1 cursor file was missing and left alone."

### WebM, MKV and converted files

For a [WebM or MKV](/projects/webm-and-matroska/), or a file [converted with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/), Frame Job copies the movie it plays from, not the file you imported. The row's [tooltip](/projects/media-tab/#the-tooltip) then says it was copied into this project's package.

## Move a consolidated package

Move or rename a consolidated package and it finds its own copies when it opens. Any missing file with a file of the same name in the package's `media` folder is pointed back at it, and a screen recording's cursor file is found again the same way.

This happens with no sheet, and it isn't an edit, so it adds no undo step. A file that still resolves is never touched, even if a file of the same name sits in `media`. Anything still missing after this brings up the [Missing media sheet](/projects/relink-media/#relink-from-the-missing-media-sheet).

## Good to know

- Nothing checks for free space first. A copy that runs out of room is reported with the files that couldn't be copied, and those files keep pointing at their originals.
- Undo points the project back at the originals but leaves the copies in the package. Consolidating again then makes second copies, such as `intro-2.mov`.
- A file that can't be copied leaves two entries that share it on the original, both of them.

## With an agent

`consolidate_media` does the same work with no sheet and no **Cancel**, and Frame Job's own window doesn't respond until the copy is done, which can take a while. On a project that has never been saved it stops and says to save first. The [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) asks you before it runs it. See [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/).

## Related

- [The Media tab](/projects/media-tab/)
- [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/)
- [Remove media](/projects/remove-media/)
- [Save, revert and close](/projects/save-and-revert/)
